title: Bayesian age-period-cohort models with bamp
text: mcmc_control("fast") runs four chains 5,000 iterations (burn-1,000, thinning 5). wrapper checks convergence bamp::checkConvergence() refits longer chains needed; stratum converge reported failed instead used. default priors second-order random walk age first-order random walks period cohort (see “Choice priors” ). Posterior medians 90% credible intervals effects (logit scale, identified bamp’s convention), Gelman-Rubin statistics chains (rhat, 1.1 converged):
code: prep <- mt_prep(step_ungroup()) set.seed(1) t0 <- proc.time() fit <- mt_fit(apc_bayes(mcmc = mcmc_control("fast")), x, prep = prep) (proc.time() - t0)[["elapsed"]] #> [1] 174.176 fit$diagnostics #>    stratum status                              message seconds #> 1:  female     ok                                       86.849 #> 2:    male     ok exposures rounded (max change 0.002)  83.735 eff <- mt_parameters(fit) eff[, .N, by = .(stratum, parameter)] #>    stratum parameter  N #> 1:  female       age 13 #> 2:  female    period 37 #> 3:  female    cohort 97 #> 4:    male       age 13 #> 5:    male    period 37 #> 6:    male    cohort 97 #> 7:  female      rhat  4 #> 8:    male      rhat  4 eff[parameter == "rhat", .(stratum, index, rhat = round(value, 3))] #>    stratum       index  rhat #> 1:  female    age_prec 1.000 #> 2:  female period_prec 1.001 #> 3:  female cohort_prec 1.000 #> 4:  female      fitted 1.003 #> 5:    male    age_prec 1.000 #> 6:    male period_prec 1.000 #> 7:    male cohort_prec 1.001 #> 8:    male      fitted 1.004 ggplot2::ggplot(eff[parameter != "rhat"], ggplot2::aes(as.numeric(index), value, colour = stratum, fill = stratum)) +   ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +   ggplot2::geom_line() +   ggplot2::facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free") +   ggplot2::labs(x = "Index (age group, period or cohort)", y = "Effect (logit scale)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +   scale_colour_mortensor(type = "categorical") +   scale_fill_mortensor(type = "categorical") +   theme_mortensor()

Deaths also cluster: epidemic, heat wave hard winter raises deaths many people cells. Li, Hardy Tan (2009) model clusters within cell whose death rates differ gamma distributed factor. Unmodelled variation. model parameters leaves part variation rates unexplained. Lee-Carter one period index, year unusual ages deviates fit. deviations look like extra variation counts around fitted means. counts overdispersed: variance exceeds mean. Smoothing age leaves almost year--year variation, 5-year age groups neighbouring ages already agree closely; matters single years age sparse data (small areas, causes death). Smoothing time surface remove year--year variation keep trend, including end decline 2011. time, smoothing parameter chosen age: 85-89, deaths many year--year variation large relative Poisson noise, smoother keeps much variation.

text: mt_smooth_check() compares smoothed observed rates: dispersion: variance observed deaths around smoothed ones, relative Poisson variance, allowing degrees freedom smoother. 1 means smoother removed Poisson noise ; 1 means also removed year effects; well 1 means followed noise. trend_ratio: variance year--year changes smoothed rates relative observed ones. title: mortensor: flexible mortality forecasting across data granularities — mortensor-package
text: Data: mt_data() stores deaths, exposures populations observed age period resolution (age_groups(), single_ages(), single_years(), parse_age_labels()); as_mt_data() mt_from_hmd() read Human Mortality Database data; mt_validate() checks plausibility; mt_example() simulates data known truth. Harmonisation: mt_regroup() aggregates exactly, mt_ungroup() estimates single-year data penalized composite link model, mt_smooth() smooths rates; mt_prep() bundles steps backtests refit every training window. Models: rwd(), lee_carter(), p_splines(), cp_splines(), arima_series(), ets_series(), hyndman_ullah(), coherent_fdm(), stmomo() (including Plat model), stanmomo(), li_lee(), coda(), bohk_rau(), nordpred_apc(), apc_bayes() (package bamp), experimental tucker3(), coda_multiway() coda_causes(), ensemble(), fitted mt_fit() (optionally tuned tuned()) forecast mt_forecast() simulated paths (mt_draws). product_ratio() cause_shares() deprecated. article "Methods sources" lists published source every method. Hierarchies: mt_hierarchy() describes crossed nested strata (example sex x region x deprivation quintile totals), mt_aggregate_strata() adds aggregates, mt_reconcile() reconciled() make forecasts add draw draw, mt_order_strata() imposes orderings. Wrappers model: ensemble(), reconciled(), recalibrated() (spread fitted recent forecast errors), anchored() (jump-observed level), bootstrapped() tuned(). Evaluation: mt_backtest() mt_score(), rates, life expectancy age-standardised rates. past: mt_observed(), mt_contrast() mt_inequality(). Derived quantities plots: life_table(), life_expectancy(), mt_deaths(), mt_plot_forecast() mt_plot_*() functions. Decomposition: mt_decompose() splits differences life expectancy summaries age, cause subgroup composition, observed data, forecasts .

"rh" StMoMo's Renshaw-Haberman model cohortAgeFun = "1" (default StMoMo's rh()): log m(x,t) = (x) + b(x) k(t) + g(t - x), cohort effect without age modulation, original 2006 specification Renshaw-Haberman model, whose cohort effect modulated second age function. Models fitted per stratum real ages (lower bounds single-year intervals; models cohort effect need single years age), deaths central exposures; logit-link models initial exposures approximated central exposures plus half deaths, forecast death probabilities converted central rates (m = -log(1 - q)). Cohorts observed fewer clip cells get zero weight; fitted rates use effect nearest estimated cohort. Draws come simulate() fitted model (period indexes simulated multivariate random walk drift, cohort index ARIMA process). Predictive draws (mt_forecast(predictive = TRUE)) add Poisson variation deaths given rates exposures, observation noise.
